claim: PomX consists of two functionally distinct domains.
source: Here, we demonstrate that PomX consists of two functionally distinct domains and has three functions.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing that PomX can be divided into N-terminal (PomXN) and C-terminal (PomXC) domains with distinct functions.

claim: The N-terminal domain of PomX stimulates ATPase activity of the ParA/MinD ATPase PomZ.
source: The N-terminal domain stimulates ATPase activity of the ParA/MinD ATPase PomZ.
evidence: The abstract states this directly and is supported by in vitro ATPase assays shown in the results.

claim: The C-terminal domain of PomX interacts with PomY and forms polymers.
source: The C-terminal domain interacts with PomY and forms polymers, which serve as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z complex formation.
evidence: The abstract states this directly and is supported by BACTH, TEM, and pull-down experiments in the results.

claim: The C-terminal domain of PomX serves as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z complex formation.
source: The C-terminal domain interacts with PomY and forms polymers, which serve as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z complex formation.
evidence: The abstract states this directly and is supported by in vivo localization and in vitro interaction studies.

claim: The PomX/PomZ interaction is important for fission of the PomX/Y/Z complex.
source: Moreover, the PomX/PomZ interaction is important for fission of the PomX/Y/Z complex.
evidence: The abstract states this directly and is supported by time-lapse microscopy data showing reduced cluster fission in PomX AAP mutants.

claim: ATPase activating proteins of ParA/MinD ATPases are highly modular.
source: These observations together with previous work support that the architecturally diverse ATPase activating proteins of ParA/MinD ATPases are highly modular and use the same mechanism to activate their cognate ATPase via a short positively charged N-terminal extension.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of PomX with other AAPs and literature citations.

claim: ATPase activating proteins of ParA/MinD ATPases use the same mechanism to activate their cognate ATPase via a short positively charged N-terminal extension.
source: These observations together with previous work support that the architecturally diverse ATPase activating proteins of ParA/MinD ATPases are highly modular and use the same mechanism to activate their cognate ATPase via a short positively charged N-terminal extension.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data on PomX and comparison with other AAPs from the literature.

claim: The PomX/Y/Z complex is approximately 15 MDa in size.
source: The Pom proteins form a dynamically localized complex with an estimated size of ~15 MDa in vivo that is visible as a cluster by epifluorescence microscopy (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: The PomX/Y/Z complex associates with the nucleoid via PomZ.
source: This complex associates with the nucleoid via PomZ, and early during the cell cycle, it is positioned on the nucleoid away from midcell, that is off-center, close to the new cell pole (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: The PomX/Y/Z complex translocates by biased random motion on the nucleoid to the midnucleoid.
source: Subsequently, the complex translocates by biased random motion on the nucleoid to the midnucleoid, which coincides with midcell.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: At midnucleoid, the PomXYZ complex undergoes constrained motion and stimulates Z-ring formation.
source: At midnucleoid, the PomXYZ complex undergoes constrained motion and stimulates Z-ring formation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: During cell division, the PomX/Y/Z complex undergoes fission, with the two portions segregating to the two daughters.
source: Intriguingly, during cell division, the PomX/Y/Z complex undergoes fission, with the two 'portions' segregating to the two daughters (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: PomX spontaneously polymerizes in a cofactor-independent manner to form filaments in vitro.
source: In vitro PomX spontaneously polymerizes in a cofactor-independent manner to form filaments, and alone forms a cluster in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: PomY bundles PomX filaments in vitro.
source: PomY bundles PomX filaments in vitro; in vivo PomY is recruited by PomX to form a PomX/Y complex, which is not associated with the nucleoid and stalled somewhere in cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: PomY is recruited by PomX to form a PomX/Y complex in vivo.
source: PomY bundles PomX filaments in vitro; in vivo PomY is recruited by PomX to form a PomX/Y complex, which is not associated with the nucleoid and stalled somewhere in cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: The PomX/Y complex is not associated with the nucleoid and is stalled somewhere in cells.
source: PomY bundles PomX filaments in vitro; in vivo PomY is recruited by PomX to form a PomX/Y complex, which is not associated with the nucleoid and stalled somewhere in cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: ATP- and DNA-bound PomZ dimers are recruited to the PomX/Y complex by interactions with PomX as well as PomY.
source: ATP- and DNA-bound PomZ dimers, but not monomeric PomZ, are recruited to the PomX/Y complex by interactions with PomX as well as PomY, resulting in the association of the PomX/Y/Z complex to the nucleoid.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: Monomeric PomZ is not recruited to the PomX/Y complex.
source: ATP- and DNA-bound PomZ dimers, but not monomeric PomZ, are recruited to the PomX/Y complex by interactions with PomX as well as PomY, resulting in the association of the PomX/Y/Z complex to the nucleoid.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: PomZ is rapidly turned over in the PomX/Y/Z complex and released in a monomeric form to the cytosol due to the AAP activity of PomX and PomY.
source: Due to the AAP activity of PomX and PomY, PomZ is rapidly turned over in the PomX/Y/Z complex and released in a monomeric form to the cytosol.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: Motion of the PomX/Y/Z complex depends on non-specific DNA binding and ATP hydrolysis by PomZ.
source: Motion of the PomX/Y/Z complex depends on non-specific DNA binding and ATP hydrolysis by PomZ (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: Translocation to midnucleoid and constrained motion at midnucleoid arise from the continuous turnover of PomZ in the complex together with the diffusive PomZ flux on the nucleoid into the PomX/Y/Z complex.
source: Translocation to midnucleoid and constrained motion at midnucleoid arise from the continuous turnover of PomZ in the complex together with the diffusive PomZ flux on the nucleoid into the PomX/Y/Z complex (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: All three Pom proteins are important for Z-ring formation at midcell.
source: Finally, while all three Pom proteins are important for Z-ring formation at midcell, PomY and PomZ in the PomX/Y/Z complex are thought to be directly involved in recruiting FtsZ to the division site based on protein-protein interaction analyses (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: PomY and PomZ in the PomX/Y/Z complex are thought to be directly involved in recruiting FtsZ to the division site.
source: Finally, while all three Pom proteins are important for Z-ring formation at midcell, PomY and PomZ in the PomX/Y/Z complex are thought to be directly involved in recruiting FtsZ to the division site based on protein-protein interaction analyses (Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: PomX homologs have an overall similar architecture with high similarity in the C-terminal regions while the N-terminal regions vary in length and similarity.
source: Although PomX homologs are of different length, their overall architecture is similar and with a high level of similarity in the C-terminal regions while the N-terminal regions vary in length and similarity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by Figure 1B showing sequence analysis.

claim: The region from residues 27 to 182 in M. xanthus PomX is Ala and Pro-rich (23% Pro; 19% Ala).
source: In M. xanthus PomX, the region from residues 27 to 182 is Ala and Pro-rich (23% Pro; 19% Ala) and the region from residues 222 to 401 contains a coiled-coil domain (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The region from residues 222 to 401 in M. xanthus PomX contains a coiled-coil domain.
source: In M. xanthus PomX, the region from residues 27 to 182 is Ala and Pro-rich (23% Pro; 19% Ala) and the region from residues 222 to 401 contains a coiled-coil domain (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: mCh-PomXWT complemented the division defect of the ΔpomX mutant.
source: mCh-PomXWT complemented the division defect of the ΔpomX mutant in agreement with previous observations (Schumacher et al., 2017), while the truncated variants did not.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to cell length measurements and previous work.

claim: The truncated PomX variants (mCh-PomXN and mCh-PomXC) did not complement the division defect of the ΔpomX mutant.
source: mCh-PomXWT complemented the division defect of the ΔpomX mutant in agreement with previous observations (Schumacher et al., 2017), while the truncated variants did not.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to cell length measurements.

claim: mCh-PomXWT formed a single well-defined cluster in 93% of ΔpomX cells and 94% of WT cells.
source: mCh-PomXWT formed a single well-defined cluster in 93% and 94% of ΔpomX and WT cells, respectively (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1E showing fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: mCh-PomXWT clusters localized in the off-center position in short cells and at midcell in long cells.
source: These clusters localized in the off-center position (defined as clusters outside the midcell region at 50 ± 5% of cell length) in short cells and at midcell in long cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1E showing fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: The truncated mCh-PomX variants (mCh-PomXN and mCh-PomXC) displayed diffuse localization in ΔpomX cells.
source: The truncated mCh-PomX variants displayed diffuse localization in ΔpomX cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1E showing fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: mCh-PomXC formed a single cluster in 90% of pomX+ cells.
source: However, mCh-PomXC but not mCh-PomXN formed a single cluster in 90% of pomX+ cells and localized as mCh-PomXWT (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1E showing fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: mCh-PomXN did not form a cluster in pomX+ cells.
source: However, mCh-PomXC but not mCh-PomXN formed a single cluster in 90% of pomX+ cells and localized as mCh-PomXWT (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1E showing fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: Cluster formation by mCh-PomXC was independent of PomY and PomZ.
source: This cluster formation by mCh-PomXC was independent of PomY and PomZ (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), supporting that mCh-PomXC is integrated into the PomX/Y/Z cluster via interaction with PomX.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 1F showing fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: mCh-PomXC is integrated into the PomX/Y/Z cluster via interaction with PomX.
source: This cluster formation by mCh-PomXC was independent of PomY and PomZ (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), supporting that mCh-PomXC is integrated into the PomX/Y/Z cluster via interaction with PomX.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the localization data.

claim: Both PomX domains are essential for function.
source: We conclude that both PomX domains are essential for function and that mCh-PomXC can integrate into the PomX/Y/Z complex via interaction with PomX while mCh-PomXN cannot.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on complementation and localization data.

claim: mCh-PomXC can integrate into the PomX/Y/Z complex via interaction with PomX.
source: We conclude that both PomX domains are essential for function and that mCh-PomXC can integrate into the PomX/Y/Z complex via interaction with PomX while mCh-PomXN cannot.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on localization data.

claim: mCh-PomXN cannot integrate into the PomX/Y/Z complex.
source: We conclude that both PomX domains are essential for function and that mCh-PomXC can integrate into the PomX/Y/Z complex via interaction with PomX while mCh-PomXN cannot.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on localization data.

claim: Full-length PomXWT self-interacted and interacted with PomY in BACTH assays.
source: In agreement with previous observations using purified proteins, full-length PomXWT self-interacted and interacted with PomY (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXC self-interacted and also interacted with full-length PomX and PomY in BACTH assays.
source: PomXC self-interacted and also interacted with full-length PomX and PomY, while PomXN neither self-interacted nor interacted with PomXWT, PomXC, or PomY.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXN neither self-interacted nor interacted with PomXWT, PomXC, or PomY in BACTH assays.
source: PomXC self-interacted and also interacted with full-length PomX and PomY, while PomXN neither self-interacted nor interacted with PomXWT, PomXC, or PomY.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXWT and PomXN interacted with PomZWT and PomZD90A in BACTH assays.
source: PomXWT and PomXN interacted with PomZWT and PomZD90A while PomXC did not; also, PomZD90A interacted more strongly with PomXN than PomZWT (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXC did not interact with PomZWT or PomZD90A in BACTH assays.
source: PomXWT and PomXN interacted with PomZWT and PomZD90A while PomXC did not; also, PomZD90A interacted more strongly with PomXN than PomZWT (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomZD90A interacted more strongly with PomXN than PomZWT in BACTH assays.
source: PomXWT and PomXN interacted with PomZWT and PomZD90A while PomXC did not; also, PomZD90A interacted more strongly with PomXN than PomZWT (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXWT-His6 formed filaments that were bundled by PomY-His6 as observed by TEM.
source: We confirmed by negative stain transmission electron microscopy (TEM) that PomXWT-His6 formed filaments that were bundled by PomY-His6, while PomY-His6 on its own did not form higher order structures (Figure 2B; Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2B showing TEM images.

claim: PomY-His6 on its own did not form higher order structures as observed by TEM.
source: We confirmed by negative stain transmission electron microscopy (TEM) that PomXWT-His6 formed filaments that were bundled by PomY-His6, while PomY-His6 on its own did not form higher order structures (Figure 2B; Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2B showing TEM images.

claim: PomXN-His6 neither formed higher-order structures by TEM nor in high-speed centrifugation experiments.
source: PomXN-His6 neither formed higher-order structures by TEM nor in high-speed centrifugation experiments (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2B and supplementary figures.

claim: PomXC-His6 spontaneously formed filaments visible by TEM.
source: Accordingly, PomXC-His6 spontaneously formed filaments visible by TEM and mostly accumulated in the pellet fraction in high-speed centrifugation experiments (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2B showing TEM images.

claim: PomY-His6 bundled the PomXC-His6 filaments as observed by TEM.
source: PomY-His6 bundled the PomXC-His6 filaments and was enriched in the pellet fraction in centrifugation assays in the presence of PomXC-His6 (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2B showing TEM images.

claim: PomXWT-His6 and PomY-His6 interact with PomXC-Strep in pull-down experiments.
source: Finally, we confirmed in pull-down experiments using truncated PomX-Strep variants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) that PomXWT-His6 and PomY-His6 interact with PomXC-Strep (Figure 2C) but not with PomXN-Strep (Figure 2D) and that PomXC-His6 did not interact with PomXN-Strep (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2C showing pull-down data.

claim: PomXWT-His6 and PomY-His6 do not interact with PomXN-Strep in pull-down experiments.
source: Finally, we confirmed in pull-down experiments using truncated PomX-Strep variants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) that PomXWT-His6 and PomY-His6 interact with PomXC-Strep (Figure 2C) but not with PomXN-Strep (Figure 2D) and that PomXC-His6 did not interact with PomXN-Strep (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2D showing pull-down data.

claim: PomXC-His6 did not interact with PomXN-Strep in pull-down experiments.
source: Finally, we confirmed in pull-down experiments using truncated PomX-Strep variants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) that PomXWT-His6 and PomY-His6 interact with PomXC-Strep (Figure 2C) but not with PomXN-Strep (Figure 2D) and that PomXC-His6 did not interact with PomXN-Strep (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to supplementary figure showing pull-down data.

claim: His6-PomZ ATP hydrolysis was stimulated twofold in the presence of saturating concentrations of DNA compared to no DNA.
source: In the presence of increasing concentrations of non-specific herring sperm DNA, His6-PomZ ATP hydrolysis was stimulated, reaching saturation at ~40 µg/ml DNA. At this concentration, His6-PomZ ATP hydrolysis was stimulated twofold (specific activity: ~15 ATP hr−1, 4 µM His6-PomZ) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2F showing ATPase assay data.

claim: PomXWT-His6 only stimulated His6-PomZ ATPase activity in the presence of DNA.
source: PomXWT-His6 only stimulated His6-PomZ ATPase activity in the presence of DNA (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2G showing ATPase assay data.

claim: PomXN-His6 stimulated His6-PomZ ATP hydrolysis in the presence of DNA as efficiently as PomXWT-His6.
source: Importantly, and in agreement with the BACTH analysis, PomXN-His6 stimulated His6-PomZ ATP hydrolysis in the presence of DNA as efficiently as PomXWT-His6 (specific activity: 43 ± 4 ATP hr−1 at 15 µM PomXN-His6, 4 µM His6-PomZ) (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2H showing ATPase assay data.

claim: PomXC-His6 did not stimulate His6-PomZ ATPase activity.
source: By contrast, PomXC-His6 did not stimulate His6-PomZ ATPase activity (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 2I showing ATPase assay data.

claim: PomX filament formation is not essential for AAP activity.
source: The observations that PomXN does not spontaneously form filaments in vitro while full-length PomX does and these two PomX variants stimulate PomZ ATPase activity with equal efficiency provide evidence that PomX filament formation is not essential for AAP activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on ATPase and TEM data.

claim: The PomXN domains in a PomX filament act independently of each other to stimulate PomZ ATPase activity.
source: These observations also strongly support that the PomXN domains in a PomX filament act independently of each other to stimulate PomZ ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on ATPase data.

claim: PomXN interacts with PomZ and harbors the entire AAP activity.
source: Altogether, we conclude that (1) PomX consists of two domains with distinct functions that are both required for PomX activity in vivo; (2) PomXN interacts with PomZ and harbors the entire AAP activity; (3) PomXC is required and sufficient to mediate PomX self-interaction with spontaneous filament formation in vitro and PomX-dependent cluster incorporation in vivo; (4) PomXC interacts with PomY; and, (5) the PomXN domains in a PomX filament function independently of each other to stimulate PomZ ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on multiple experimental approaches.

claim: PomXC is required and sufficient to mediate PomX self-interaction with spontaneous filament formation in vitro and PomX-dependent cluster incorporation in vivo.
source: Altogether, we conclude that (1) PomX consists of two domains with distinct functions that are both required for PomX activity in vivo; (2) PomXN interacts with PomZ and harbors the entire AAP activity; (3) PomXC is required and sufficient to mediate PomX self-interaction with spontaneous filament formation in vitro and PomX-dependent cluster incorporation in vivo; (4) PomXC interacts with PomY; and, (5) the PomXN domains in a PomX filament function independently of each other to stimulate PomZ ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on multiple experimental approaches.

claim: PomXC interacts with PomY.
source: Altogether, we conclude that (1) PomX consists of two domains with distinct functions that are both required for PomX activity in vivo; (2) PomXN interacts with PomZ and harbors the entire AAP activity; (3) PomXC is required and sufficient to mediate PomX self-interaction with spontaneous filament formation in vitro and PomX-dependent cluster incorporation in vivo; (4) PomXC interacts with PomY; and, (5) the PomXN domains in a PomX filament function independently of each other to stimulate PomZ ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on multiple experimental approaches.

claim: PomXNPEP (residues 1-22) is enriched in charged amino acids, six of which are positively charged.
source: This analysis revealed a stretch of highly conserved amino acids at the N-terminus (residues 1–22, from hereon PomXNPEP) that is enriched in charged amino acids, six of which are positively charged (Figures 1B and 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to sequence analysis figures.

claim: Lys13 and Arg15 in PomXNPEP are important for PomX function.
source: We conclude that Lys13 and Arg15 in PomXNPEP are important for PomX function.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on cell length and division phenotype data.

claim: Substitution of Lys13 and/or Arg15 does not result in a complete loss of PomX function.
source: Because the PomXK13A, PomXR15A, and PomXK13AR15A variants caused defects distinct from the ΔpomX mutant, i.e., cells are shorter, and with more constrictions, we conclude that substitution of Lys13 and/or Arg15 does not result in a complete loss of PomX function (see Discussion).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on phenotypic analysis.

claim: mCh-PomXK13A, mCh-PomXR15A, and mCh-PomXK13AR15A are functional in forming clusters, defining the division site, and stimulating division but cannot correctly position the division site at midcell.
source: Overall, these observations demonstrate that mCh-PomXK13A, mCh-PomXR15A, and mCh-PomXK13AR15A are functional in forming clusters, defining the division site, and stimulating division but cannot correctly position the division site at midcell.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on localization and division data.

claim: PomXNPEP is required for the interaction between PomX and PomZ but not for PomX self-interaction or PomX interaction with PomY.
source: Altogether, these observations support that PomXNPEP is required for the interaction between PomX and PomZ but for neither PomX self-interaction nor PomX interaction with PomY.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on BACTH and localization data.

claim: PomZ in its ATP-bound dimeric form can be recruited independently by PomX and PomY to the PomX/Y complex.
source: Finally, they support that PomZ in its ATP-bound dimeric form can be recruited independently by PomX and PomY to the PomX/Y complex.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on localization data with PomZD90A.

claim: PomXK13AR15A and PomXΔ2-21 self-interacted, and also interacted with PomXWT and PomY in BACTH assays.
source: PomXK13AR15A and PomXΔ2-21 self-interacted, and also interacted with PomXWT and PomY (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXK13AR15A-His6 formed filaments that were bundled by PomY-His6 in vitro.
source: Consistently, in vitro PomXK13AR15A-His6 formed filaments that were bundled by PomY-His6, accumulated in the pellet fraction after high-speed centrifugation, and brought PomY-His6 to the pellet fraction similarly to PomXWT-His6 (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5B showing TEM data.

claim: Neither PomXN_Δ2-21 nor PomXN_K13AR15A interacted with PomXWT and PomY in BACTH assays.
source: As expected, in the BACTH neither PomXN_ Δ2-21 nor PomXN_K13AR15A interacted with PomXWT and PomY (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5A showing BACTH data.

claim: All four PomXNPEP variants (PomXΔ2-21, PomXN_Δ2-21, PomXK13AR15A and PomXN_K13AR15A) were dramatically reduced in interaction with PomZ and PomZD90A in BACTH assays.
source: Importantly, all four PomXNPEP variants (PomXΔ2-21, PomXN_Δ2-21, PomXK13AR15A and PomXN_K13AR15A) were dramatically reduced in interaction with PomZ and PomZD90A (Figure 5A; see also Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5A showing BACTH data.

claim: PomXNPEP is specifically important for the PomX/PomZ interaction and not for PomX/PomX and PomX/PomY interactions.
source: Altogether, these findings further support that PomXNPEP is specifically important for the PomX/PomZ interaction and not for PomX/PomX and PomX/PomY interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on BACTH data.

claim: Neither PomXK13AR15A-His6 nor PomXN_K13AR15A-His6 stimulated PomZ ATPase activity.
source: Remarkably, neither PomXK13AR15A-His6 nor PomXN_K13AR15A-His6 stimulated PomZ ATPase activity (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5D showing ATPase assay data.

claim: The PomXNPEP peptide alone stimulated His6-PomZ ATPase activity in the presence of DNA.
source: The PomXNPEP peptide alone stimulated His6-PomZ ATPase activity in the presence of DNA (specific activity: 27 ± 5 ATP hr−1 at 15 µM PomXNPEP, 4 µM His6-PomZ) while a PomXNPEP peptide with the K13AR15A substitutions did not (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5E showing ATPase assay data.

claim: A PomXNPEP peptide with the K13AR15A substitutions did not stimulate His6-PomZ ATPase activity.
source: The PomXNPEP peptide alone stimulated His6-PomZ ATPase activity in the presence of DNA (specific activity: 27 ± 5 ATP hr−1 at 15 µM PomXNPEP, 4 µM His6-PomZ) while a PomXNPEP peptide with the K13AR15A substitutions did not (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 5E showing ATPase assay data.

claim: PomXNPEP is required and sufficient for stimulation of PomZ ATPase activity by PomX.
source: We conclude that PomXNPEP is required and sufficient for stimulation of PomZ ATPase activity by PomX.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on ATPase assay data.

claim: In the presence of mCh-PomXWT, approximately 80% of divisions are accompanied by symmetric or asymmetric cluster fission.
source: In the presence of mCh-PomXWT, ~80% of divisions are accompanied by symmetric or asymmetric cluster fission, with each portion of a divided cluster segregating to a daughter (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 6A,B showing time-lapse microscopy data.

claim: mCh-PomXK13AR15A clusters showed cluster fission and segregation to daughters in only approximately 20% of cells.
source: mCh-PomXK13AR15A clusters showed the same three patterns during division. However, cluster fission and segregation to daughters occurred in only ~20% of cells (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 6A,B showing time-lapse microscopy data.

claim: In ΔpomZ cells, mCh-PomXWT clusters rarely underwent fission and mostly segregated into one daughter.
source: In ΔpomZ cells, division occurs at a reduced frequency but still over the PomX/Y cluster (Schumacher et al., 2017). In these cells, mCh-PomXWT clusters rarely underwent fission and mostly segregated into one daughter (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 6A,B showing time-lapse microscopy data.

claim: In cells with PomZD90A, approximately 80% of clusters underwent fission during division and segregated to both daughters.
source: In cells with PomZD90A, divisions also occurred over the cluster, and ~80% of clusters underwent fission during division and segregated to both daughters (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to Figure 6A,B showing time-lapse microscopy data.

claim: The interaction between PomZ and PomX is important for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission, while ATP hydrolysis by PomZ is not.
source: Altogether, these observations suggest that the interaction between PomZ and PomX is important for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission, while ATP hydrolysis by PomZ is not.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the results based on time-lapse microscopy data.

claim: PomX is a triple regulator of cell division.
source: In the present study, we used in vivo and in vitro approaches to functionally dissect the cell division regulatory protein PomX. We demonstrate that PomX is composed of two domains and has three functions in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The N-terminal PomXN domain contains the PomZ AAP activity.
source: The N-terminal PomXN domain contains the PomZ AAP activity; the C-terminal PomXC domain is essential for PomX self-interaction, for the interaction with PomY, and functions as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z cluster formation; and, the PomX/Z interaction, but not PomZ ATPase activity, is important for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission during division.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The C-terminal PomXC domain is essential for PomX self-interaction, for the interaction with PomY, and functions as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z cluster formation.
source: The N-terminal PomXN domain contains the PomZ AAP activity; the C-terminal PomXC domain is essential for PomX self-interaction, for the interaction with PomY, and functions as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z cluster formation; and, the PomX/Z interaction, but not PomZ ATPase activity, is important for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission during division.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The PomX/Z interaction, but not PomZ ATPase activity, is important for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission during division.
source: The N-terminal PomXN domain contains the PomZ AAP activity; the C-terminal PomXC domain is essential for PomX self-interaction, for the interaction with PomY, and functions as a scaffold for PomX/Y/Z cluster formation; and, the PomX/Z interaction, but not PomZ ATPase activity, is important for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission during division.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: PomXN is Ala/Pro-rich and likely unstructured.
source: PomXN, which is Ala/Pro-rich and, therefore, likely unstructured, interacts with PomZ and activates ATPase activity of DNA-bound PomZ in vitro as efficiently as PomXWT.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on sequence composition.

claim: A peptide comprising the N-terminal 22 residues of PomX (PomXNPEP) is sufficient to activate PomZ ATPase activity.
source: Moreover, a peptide comprising the N-terminal 22 residues of PomX (PomXNPEP) is sufficient to activate PomZ ATPase activity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on ATPase assay data.

claim: In PomXNPEP, two positively charged residues (Lys13 and Arg15) are essential for AAP activity.
source: In PomXNPEP, two positively charged residues (Lys13 and Arg15) are essential for AAP activity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on ATPase assay data.

claim: The AAP activity of PomXNPEP was lower than that of PomXN.
source: Of note, the AAP activity of PomXNPEP was lower than that of PomXN.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on ATPase assay data.

claim: PomXWT serves as a scaffold protein for cluster formation in vivo.
source: Because PomXWT alone can form a cluster and is essential for PomX/Y/Z cluster formation in vivo, these observations support a model whereby PomXWT serves as a scaffold protein for cluster formation in vivo and in which PomXC has a key role in this scaffolding function by self-interacting and interacting with PomY.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a model based on experimental data.

claim: PomXC has a key role in the scaffolding function by self-interacting and interacting with PomY.
source: Because PomXWT alone can form a cluster and is essential for PomX/Y/Z cluster formation in vivo, these observations support a model whereby PomXWT serves as a scaffold protein for cluster formation in vivo and in which PomXC has a key role in this scaffolding function by self-interacting and interacting with PomY.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a model based on experimental data.

claim: PomXWT monomers in vivo interact via their coiled-coil domain in PomXC to spontaneously form a polymeric structure that is stabilized or modified by PomXN.
source: Altogether, we suggest that PomXWT monomers in vivo interact via their coiled-coil domain in PomXC to spontaneously form a polymeric structure that is stabilized or modified by PomXN; this polymeric structure, in turn, serves as a scaffold to recruit PomY resulting in formation of the PomX/Y complex.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a model based on experimental data.

claim: The polymeric structure formed by PomXWT serves as a scaffold to recruit PomY resulting in formation of the PomX/Y complex.
source: Altogether, we suggest that PomXWT monomers in vivo interact via their coiled-coil domain in PomXC to spontaneously form a polymeric structure that is stabilized or modified by PomXN; this polymeric structure, in turn, serves as a scaffold to recruit PomY resulting in formation of the PomX/Y complex.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a model based on experimental data.

claim: PomXWT monomers in the polymeric structure in vitro and cluster in vivo stimulate PomZ ATPase activity independently of each other.
source: Because PomXWT and the likely unstructured PomXN stimulate PomZ ATPase activity to the same extent, these observations also strongly support that PomXWT monomers in the polymeric structure in vitro and cluster in vivo stimulate PomZ ATPase activity independently of each other.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from ATPase data.

claim: Spontaneous polymerization of PomXWT ensures that one, and only one, PomX scaffold is formed per cell in vivo.
source: We speculate that this spontaneous polymerization ensures that one, and only one, PomX scaffold is formed per cell in vivo, thus guaranteeing that only one PomX/Y/Z complex is formed per cell as would be required for a complex that defines the site of cell division.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on experimental observations.

claim: PomZ ATPase activity is essential for PomX/Y/Z cluster translocation and cluster localization to midcell.
source: By analyzing PomZ variants, we previously showed that PomZ ATPase activity is essential for PomX/Y/Z cluster translocation and cluster localization to midcell.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with reference to previous work.

claim: The low intrinsic PomZ ATPase activity is not sufficient to fuel translocation of the PomX/Y/Z cluster to midcell.
source: Because the PomX variants with reduced AAP activity resulted in the formation of PomX/Y/Z clusters that were typically not at midcell, we conclude that the low intrinsic PomZ ATPase activity is not sufficient to fuel translocation of the PomX/Y/Z cluster to midcell and that this translocation is fueled by PomX, and likely also by PomY, stimulated ATP hydrolysis by PomZ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on localization data.

claim: Translocation of the PomX/Y/Z cluster to midcell is fueled by PomX, and likely also by PomY, stimulated ATP hydrolysis by PomZ.
source: Because the PomX variants with reduced AAP activity resulted in the formation of PomX/Y/Z clusters that were typically not at midcell, we conclude that the low intrinsic PomZ ATPase activity is not sufficient to fuel translocation of the PomX/Y/Z cluster to midcell and that this translocation is fueled by PomX, and likely also by PomY, stimulated ATP hydrolysis by PomZ.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on localization data.

claim: PomX AAP mutants are fully competent in stimulating cell division but deficient in positioning the PomX/Y/Z cluster at midcell.
source: Thus, PomX AAP mutants are fully competent in stimulating cell division but deficient in positioning the PomX/Y/Z cluster at midcell.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on phenotypic data.

claim: PomX-stimulated PomZ ATPase activity is not important for stimulation of Z-ring formation.
source: These observations also support that PomX-stimulated PomZ ATPase activity is not important for stimulation of Z-ring formation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from phenotypic data.

claim: PomX AAP mutants retain partial PomX activity.
source: In cells lacking the PomX protein, PomY and PomZ do not form clusters and cell divisions occur at a low frequency (Schumacher et al., 2017); by contrast, the PomX AAP mutants still support PomX/Y/Z cluster formation and cell division. Thus, PomX AAP mutants retain partial PomX activity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on phenotypic comparison.

claim: The division defects in Δpom mutants are a consequence of reduced formation and mislocalization of division constrictions.
source: Thus, the division defects in Δpom mutants are a consequence of reduced formation and mislocalization of division constrictions, while the PomX AAP mutants are only deficient in cell division localization.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on phenotypic comparison.

claim: The PomX AAP mutants are only deficient in cell division localization.
source: Thus, the division defects in Δpom mutants are a consequence of reduced formation and mislocalization of division constrictions, while the PomX AAP mutants are only deficient in cell division localization.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on phenotypic comparison.

claim: DNA binding by PomZ is important for the low intrinsic as well as PomX-stimulated ATPase activity.
source: DNA binding by PomZ is important for the low intrinsic as well as PomX-stimulated ATPase activity. This is similar to what has been described for several DNA-binding ParA ATPases and their partner AAPs (Ah-Seng et al., 2009; Kiekebusch et al., 2012; Leonard et al., 2005; Lim et al., 2014; Scholefield et al., 2011; Schumacher et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on ATPase assay data and comparison with literature.

claim: PomX is the fourth type of ParA/MinD AAP that displays a characteristic N-terminus enriched in positively charged residues and in which positively charged residues are important for AAP activity.
source: Thus, PomX is the fourth type of ParA/MinD AAP that displays this characteristic N-terminus and in which positively charged residues are important for AAP activity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on comparison with other AAPs.

claim: Many AAPs of ParA/MinD ATPases use the same mechanism to stimulate ATPase activity.
source: Altogether, these findings lend further support to the notion that many AAPs of ParA/MinD ATPases use the same mechanism to stimulate ATPase activity (Leonard et al., 2005; Park et al., 2011; Zhang and Schumacher, 2017; Barillà et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on comparison with other AAPs and literature.

claim: ParA/MinD AAPs display remarkable plasticity and modularity in which a stretch of N-terminal amino acids enriched in positively charged residues grafted onto an interaction domain can generate an AAP.
source: Moreover, they support that ParA/MinD AAPs display remarkable plasticity and modularity in which a stretch of N-terminal amino acids enriched in positively charged residues grafted onto an interaction domain, which is involved in protein-protein, protein-DNA, or protein-membrane interaction, can generate an AAP.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from comparison with other AAPs.

claim: PomY does not have an N-terminus enriched in positively charged residues suggesting that its mode of action could be different from that of previously described AAPs.
source: Interestingly, PomY, the second AAP of PomZ (Schumacher et al., 2017), does not have an N-terminus enriched in positively charged residues suggesting that its mode of action could be different from that of previously described AAPs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on sequence analysis.

claim: Systems incorporating a DNA-binding ParA ATPase and an AAP(s) share similarities in their translocation.
source: In addition to similarities at the biochemical level, systems incorporating a DNA-binding ParA ATPase and an AAP(s) also share similarities in their translocation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on comparison with other systems.

claim: The PomX/Y complex, ParB-parS complexes, cytoplasmic chemoreceptor clusters and carboxysomes are all large structures that are translocated as cargo on the nucleoid in a mechanism that depends on an AAP(s) stimulating ATP hydrolysis by the cognate DNA-binding ParA ATPase.
source: The PomX/Y complex, ParB-parS complexes, cytoplasmic chemoreceptor clusters and carboxysomes are all large structures that are translocated as cargo on the nucleoid in a mechanism that depends on an AAP(s) stimulating ATP hydrolysis by the cognate DNA-binding ParA ATPase.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on comparison with other systems.

claim: The AAP(s) is an integral part of the translocated cargo in systems with DNA-binding ParA ATPases.
source: Importantly, the AAP(s) is an integral part of the translocated cargo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on comparison with other systems.

claim: The integration of the AAP activity into a large cargo structure provides an elegant solution to guarantee that ATPase activation is spatially restricted to the transported cargo.
source: We speculate that the integration of the AAP activity into a large cargo structure provides an elegant solution to guarantee that ATPase activation is spatially restricted to the transported cargo.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on comparison with other systems.

claim: Cell division is essential for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission.
source: Additionally, in cells treated with cephalexin, which blocks cell division, cluster fission also does not occur (Schumacher et al., 2017; Treuner-Lange et al., 2013). Because cephalexin-treated cells still segregate their chromosomes (Schumacher et al., 2017; Treuner-Lange et al., 2013), these observations support that cell division is essential for fission, chromosome segregation is not sufficient, and the PomX/Z interaction is important while PomZ ATPase activity is not.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on experimental data and literature.

claim: Chromosome segregation is not sufficient for PomX/Y/Z cluster fission.
source: Additionally, in cells treated with cephalexin, which blocks cell division, cluster fission also does not occur (Schumacher et al., 2017; Treuner-Lange et al., 2013). Because cephalexin-treated cells still segregate their chromosomes (Schumacher et al., 2017; Treuner-Lange et al., 2013), these observations support that cell division is essential for fission, chromosome segregation is not sufficient, and the PomX/Z interaction is important while PomZ ATPase activity is not.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion based on experimental data and literature.

claim: The splitting of plasmid clusters and PomX/Y/Z cluster fission may occur by different mechanisms.
source: This is in contrast to the SopB/SopA system for plasmid F segregation. For this system, it has been shown that SopB-stimulated ATPase activity of SopA is important to split plasmid clusters (Ah-Seng et al., 2013) suggesting that the splitting of plasmid clusters and PomX/Y/Z cluster fission may occur by different mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation based on comparison with another system.
